name: Gazzam
overview: Gazzam was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role was connected to the religious duties associated with the temple, reflecting the Levitical responsibility in worship and service. Scripture specifically identifies him in the context of the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Gazzam is a proper name that means some kind of bird or insect. While the name was not given by God, it is recorded in Scripture, emphasizing his individual identity among the Levites.
familyAndRelationships: Gazzam is identified as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical lineage. Beyond this tribal connection, Scripture does not provide additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Gazzam's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi during the post-exilic period. His mention highlights the restoration of temple service and the reestablishment of worship practices following the return from exile, underscoring the faithfulness of God's people in maintaining their covenantal duties.
